title: mintFor() ignores per-dispatcher disabled flag, allowing minting to disabled dispatchers
description: NFTMinterV2.mintFor() checks only that the dispatcher is registered (`configs[index].dispatcher != address(0)`) but does not check the `disabled` flag. The paid mint path (_executeMint) correctly enforces `require(!config.disabled)` at line 174. Since the NFTMigrator is an authorized minter and calls mintFor(), users can migrate V1 NFTs into V2 dispatcher indexes that the owner has explicitly disabled. The disabled flag exists to allow the owner to halt minting for specific dispatchers (e.g., if a dispatcher has a vulnerability), but mintFor() completely bypasses this control.
impact: Owner's intent to disable a dispatcher is not respected for the mintFor path. If a V2 dispatcher is disabled because of a discovered issue, migration can still mint NFTs pointing to that disabled dispatcher. This inflates V2 supply in categories the owner explicitly halted and may expose users to NFTs linked to compromised dispatchers.
attack_path: Owner discovers issue with V2 dispatcher at index 2.
Owner calls setDispatcherDisabled(2, true) to halt minting.
Regular mints to index 2 are correctly blocked by _executeMint.
User holding V1 NFTs mapped to index 2 calls NFTMigrator.migrate().
NFTMigrator calls v2.mintFor(2, user) -- no disabled check.
V2 NFT is minted for the disabled dispatcher.
recommendation: Add `require(!configs[index].disabled, "NFTMinterV2: dispatcher is disabled");` to mintFor(), matching the check in _executeMint().
